questions.q: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of India for a year measures the
o: market value of all goods and services, including intermediate goods, produced by Indian citizens anywhere in the world during the year
total income earned by Indian residents from domestic and foreign sources during the year, net of depreciation
market value of all final goods and services sold, including second-hand goods, in India during the year
market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of India during the year, irrespective of who owns the factors of production
questions.e: GDP follows the territorial principle: it counts final output produced inside the country whoever owns the firm. Counting intermediate goods would double count, and second-hand sales are not current production.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross National Product (GNP) is equal to GDP plus Net Factor Income from Abroad.
2. Net National Product at market prices is equal to GNP at market prices minus depreciation.
3. Net National Product at factor cost is equal to NNP at market prices plus net indirect taxes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GNP adds NFIA to GDP, and NNP deducts depreciation (consumption of fixed capital) from GNP. Statement 3 is reversed: moving from market prices to factor cost means subtracting net indirect taxes (indirect taxes minus subsidies), because factor cost is what the factors actually receive.
questions.h: Factor cost = Market price MINUS net indirect taxes: the government takes its cut before the factors get paid.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the national accounts:
1. Gross Value Added at basic prices equals GDP at market prices minus product taxes plus product subsidies.
2. With the 2015 revision (base year 2011-12), GDP at market prices became the headline measure of the size of the economy, replacing GDP at factor cost.
3. Gross Value Added at factor cost and Gross Value Added at basic prices are the same.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Basic prices include other taxes on production (such as land revenue or stamp duty) less other subsidies on production, which factor cost excludes, so statement 3 is wrong. Statements 1 and 2 describe the 2015 revision correctly.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Item : Treatment in estimation of national income
1. Imputed rent of owner-occupied houses : Included
2. Sale of a second-hand car : Excluded (only the dealer's commission is counted)
3. Scholarship paid by the government to students : Included
4. Self-consumed output of farm households : Included
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: A scholarship is a transfer payment: no good or service is produced in exchange, so it is excluded. Imputed rent, self-consumed farm produce and the dealer's margin on a second-hand sale reflect current production and are counted.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The National Income Committee (1949) was headed by V.K.R.V. Rao.
2. Dadabhai Naoroji made one of the earliest estimates of India's national income, in his work Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.
3. V.K.R.V. Rao made the first scientific estimate of India's national income, for 1931-32.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1949 National Income Committee was chaired by P.C. Mahalanobis, with D.R. Gadgil and V.K.R.V. Rao as members, and it produced the first official estimates. Naoroji (1867-68) and Rao (1931-32) were the pre-independence estimators.
questions.h: Mahalanobis chaired 1949; Rao was a member, not the chair.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The sale of a second-hand car in 2026 is not included in India's GDP for 2026, except for the commission earned by the dealer.
Statement-II: GDP measures only the value of goods and services newly produced in the given year.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A second-hand sale only transfers ownership of something produced in an earlier year, so its value was already counted then. The dealer's commission is a current service and is counted.

questions.q: In the expenditure approach to India's GDP, which one of the following is the largest component?
o: Net exports of goods and services
questions.e: Household spending is more than half of India's GDP, ahead of gross fixed capital formation (investment) at roughly a third. Government consumption is around a tenth and net exports are negative for India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Services is the largest contributor to India's Gross Value Added.
2. Agriculture and allied activities account for a smaller share of India's workforce than of its Gross Value Added.
3. Agriculture's share in India's Gross Value Added is smaller than that of industry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Services contribute more than half of GVA and agriculture contributes well under a fifth, less than industry. Agriculture still employs roughly 45 percent of workers, so its share in employment is far larger than in GVA; statement 2 reverses this. This gap explains low farm productivity.
questions.s: Economic Survey; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q: In India, official estimates of GDP and other national accounts aggregates are compiled and released by the
o: Reserve Bank of India through its Department of Statistics and Information Management
NITI Aayog through its Data Management and Analysis Division
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
National Statistics Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.e: The National Statistics Office (formed in 2019 by merging the CSO and NSSO) compiles GDP, GVA and quarterly estimates. The RBI, NITI Aayog and the Finance Ministry use these numbers but do not produce them.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the GDP deflator:
1. It is the ratio of nominal GDP to real GDP, multiplied by 100.
2. It includes the prices of imported consumer goods bought by households.
3. Its basket covers goods and services produced domestically, including capital goods and government services, and is not restricted to items households consume.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The deflator is nominal/real x 100 and covers everything produced within the economy, with a basket that changes as output changes. Imports are not produced domestically, so their prices enter CPI but not the GDP deflator; this is the key difference between the two.
questions.h: Deflator = what we PRODUCE; CPI = what we CONSUME (including imports).

questions.q: In a year, nominal GDP of an economy is Rs 330 lakh crore and the GDP deflator is 110 (base year = 100). The real GDP of the economy in base-year prices is
questions.e: Real GDP = nominal GDP / deflator x 100 = 330/110 x 100 = 300. A deflator above 100 means prices have risen since the base year, so nominal GDP overstates real output.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India's Net Factor Income from Abroad has generally been negative, so its GNP is lower than its GDP.
2. GNP is measured on the territorial principle while GDP is measured on the nationality principle.
3. Interest earned by Indian residents on deposits held abroad is added to GDP to arrive at GNP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Profits and interest paid to foreign investors have exceeded what Indians earn abroad, so NFIA is negative and GNP < GDP. GNP counts income of a country's normal residents anywhere, while GDP counts production inside its borders; statement 2 swaps them.

questions.q: Which one of the following is counted as a factor income in the estimation of national income?
o: Old-age pension paid to a senior citizen under a social assistance scheme
Rent received by a landowner for leasing out agricultural land
Money gifted by a father to his son
questions.e: Factor incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) are payments for productive services. Pensions under social assistance, gifts and lottery winnings are transfers: nothing is produced in return.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A rise in GDP does not necessarily mean a rise in the economic welfare of the people.
Statement-II: GDP does not capture unpaid household work, nor does it deduct the cost of environmental degradation caused by production.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: GDP counts only market-valued output, so welfare-relevant things outside the market (unpaid care work, clean air) are missed, while pollution-generating output raises GDP. This is why Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q: Green GDP is arrived at by
o: adding to GDP the value of forest cover and carbon sequestered each year
deducting from GDP the value of imports of fossil fuels
computing GDP only for the renewable energy and agriculture sectors
deducting from GDP the monetary value of depletion of natural resources and environmental degradation
questions.e: Green GDP adjusts the national accounts for the natural capital used up in producing output, in the same way that depreciation is deducted for physical capital. It is not an additive measure of ecosystem benefits.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Per capita income in official Indian statistics is usually reported as Net National Income divided by the population.
2. The National Statistics Office uses purchasing power parity (PPP) conversion to publish its headline per capita income.
3. Per capita real income is obtained by dividing real Net National Income by the population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MoSPI reports per capita NNI at current and constant prices. PPP-adjusted incomes are compiled by the IMF and World Bank for cross-country comparison, not by the NSO for its headline figure.

questions.q:
Which of the following changes accompanied the 2015 revision of India's national accounts (base year 2011-12)?
1. The base year was shifted from 1999-2000 to 2011-12.
2. Gross Value Added at basic prices was introduced as the measure of sectoral output.
3. Corporate sector estimates drew on the MCA-21 database of company filings.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The 2015 series replaced the 2004-05 base (not 1999-2000), introduced GVA at basic prices and moved to company-level data from MCA-21, which better captured the corporate sector.

questions.q: In an economy, GDP at market prices is Rs 500 crore, depreciation is Rs 40 crore, net factor income from abroad is minus Rs 10 crore and net indirect taxes are Rs 30 crore. Net National Product at factor cost is
questions.e: GNP at market prices = 500 - 10 = 490; NNP at market prices = 490 - 40 = 450; NNP at factor cost = 450 - 30 = 420. The common slip is stopping at 450, which is still at market prices.

questions.q: In national income accounting, 'investment' refers to
o: purchase of shares of a company in the secondary market
purchase of a newly constructed house by a household
purchase of government bonds by a household
deposit of savings in a bank fixed deposit
questions.e: Investment means addition to the physical capital stock (capital formation), and new residential construction qualifies. Buying shares or bonds only shifts financial claims between people and creates no new capital.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the product method, only final goods or the value added at each stage should be counted, to avoid double counting.
2. In the expenditure method, imports are subtracted because they are included in consumption, investment or government spending but were not produced domestically.
3. In the expenditure method, subsidies paid by the government are included in government final consumption expenditure.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Government final consumption covers spending on goods and services the government itself uses; subsidies and pensions are transfer payments and are not part of it. Statements 1 and 2 are the standard logic of the product and expenditure methods.

questions.q: Personal disposable income is obtained by
o: subtracting personal direct taxes from personal income
adding corporate profit taxes to personal income
adding indirect taxes to personal income
questions.e: Disposable income is what households can actually spend or save after paying direct taxes such as income tax. Indirect taxes are paid on spending and are already reflected in prices.

questions.q: Who among the following was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics for developing a system of national accounts, which became the basis of the UN System of National Accounts?
questions.e: Richard Stone won the 1984 prize for his accounting framework behind the SNA. Kuznets (Nobel 1971) pioneered national income estimation in the US in the 1930s and Leontief won for input-output analysis; Keynes died before the prize existed.

questions.q: In the national accounts classification used in India, which one of the following activities is grouped under 'Industry' rather than 'Services'?
questions.e: Industry covers mining and quarrying, manufacturing, electricity-gas-water supply and other utilities, and construction. The other three options sit in the services group.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Net Domestic Product is a better indicator than GDP of the output that can be sustained without running down the capital stock.
Statement-II: Net Domestic Product is obtained after deducting consumption of fixed capital (depreciation) from GDP.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Gross measures include output needed just to replace worn-out capital. NDP removes that replacement, so what is left is the output available for consumption and net new investment.

questions.q: In a year, India's real GDP at market prices grows faster than its real Gross Value Added at basic prices. The most likely explanation is that
o: depreciation of capital stock grew faster than GVA
net product taxes (product taxes less product subsidies) in real terms grew faster than GVA
net factor income from abroad turned positive
the GDP deflator was lower than the GVA deflator in the base year
questions.e: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes - product subsidies. If subsidies are trimmed or tax collections rise faster than output, GDP growth outpaces GVA growth. NFIA and depreciation affect GNP and NDP, not GDP.

questions.q: Which one of the following sets of indicators is used by UNDP to compute the Human Development Index in its current methodology?
o: Infant mortality rate, adult literacy rate and per capita net national product
Life expectancy at birth, adult literacy and gross enrolment ratio, and GDP per capita (PPP)
Life expectancy at birth, mean and expected years of schooling, and Gross National Income per capita (PPP)
Life expectancy at age one, mean years of schooling and share of population above poverty line
questions.e: The HDI has three dimensions: a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living. Adult literacy and gross enrolment were replaced by mean and expected years of schooling, and GDP per capita by GNI per capita, in the 2010 revision.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Human Development Index:
1. It is calculated using the geometric mean of normalised dimension indices.
2. It was introduced in the first Human Development Report in 1990, associated with Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen.
3. The Human Development Report is published by the World Bank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Human Development Report is a UNDP publication, not a World Bank one. The geometric mean has been used since 2010; before it, an arithmetic mean was used.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Index/Report)
A. Gender Development Index
B. Global Gender Gap Index
C. Global Multidimensional Poverty Index
D. World Happiness Report
List-II (Publisher)
1. World Economic Forum
2. UNDP
3. UNDP and Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative
4. UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The GDI is part of the UNDP's HDR, the gender gap index belongs to the WEF, the global MPI is a UNDP-OPHI product, and the World Happiness Report comes from the UN SDSN.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: The HDI uses the geometric mean rather than the arithmetic mean of its three dimension indices.
Statement-II: The geometric mean makes it harder for high achievement in one dimension to fully compensate for poor achievement in another.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: With an arithmetic mean, high income could offset poor health or schooling one-for-one. The geometric mean penalises imbalance, reflecting the idea that the dimensions are not perfectly substitutable.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about gender-related indices of UNDP:
1. The Gender Inequality Index reflects inequality in reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market.
2. The Gender Development Index is the ratio of female HDI to male HDI.
3. A Gender Inequality Index value of 1 represents perfect gender equality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The GII is an inequality measure, so 0 means no inequality and 1 means the worst inequality; statement 3 reverses it. The GDI compares the HDI of women and men directly.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) of NITI Aayog:
1. It has three equally weighted dimensions: health, education and standard of living.
2. It uses 12 indicators, two more than the global MPI.
3. Its baseline report was based on NFHS-5 data.
4. A person is identified as multidimensionally poor if deprived in at least one-third of the weighted indicators.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The baseline report (November 2021) used NFHS-4 (2015-16); NFHS-5 data came in the later progress review. The other three statements describe the national MPI structure correctly.
questions.s: NITI Aayog, National MPI Baseline Report 2021

questions.q: Which two indicators were added in India's national MPI over the 10 indicators of the global MPI?
questions.e: The national MPI adds maternal health (under health) and bank account (under standard of living). The other options are already in the global MPI.
questions.s: NITI Aayog, National MPI Baseline Report 2021

questions.q:
Which of the following were introduced by UNDP in the Human Development Report 2010?
1. Inequality-adjusted HDI
2. Gender Inequality Index
3. Multidimensional Poverty Index
4. Gender Development Index
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The 2010 report introduced the IHDI, GII and MPI (the MPI replacing the Human Poverty Index). The Gender Development Index is older, dating to the 1995 report.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter
questions.h: 2010 = the 'I' year: IHDI, Inequality (GII), Index of poverty (MPI).

questions.q: According to Amartya Sen, development is best understood as
o: a sustained rise in per capita income and capital accumulation
the expansion of the substantive freedoms and capabilities that people have reason to value
the shift of surplus labour from the traditional to the modern sector
the trickling down of benefits of growth from higher to lower income groups
questions.e: In Development as Freedom (1999) Sen treated income as a means, not the end. The other options describe growth-centred views, such as the Lewis model and the trickle-down approach.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q: The theme 'Growth with Social Justice and Equity' is associated with which Five Year Plan of India?
questions.e: The Ninth Plan (1997-2002) emphasised growth with social justice and equity. The Eleventh Plan spoke of 'faster and more inclusive growth' and the Twelfth of 'faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth'.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q: The international process that led to the formulation of the Sustainable Development Goals was launched at the
o: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development (Rio+20), 2012
United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (Earth Summit), 1992
World Summit on Sustainable Development, Johannesburg, 2002
questions.e: Rio+20 resolved to create an open working group to propose SDGs that would carry on from the MDGs after 2015. The goals were then adopted by the UN General Assembly in September 2015.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals:
1. There are 17 goals and 169 targets.
2. They were adopted in 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda by the UN General Assembly.
3. They are legally binding on all member states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2030 Agenda is a voluntary, non-binding framework; each country sets its own national targets and reports through voluntary reviews. The count of 17 goals and 169 targets and the 2015 adoption are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
SDG : Goal
1. Goal 7 : Affordable and clean energy
2. Goal 10 : Reduced inequalities
3. Goal 12 : Climate action
4. Goal 14 : Life on land
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Climate action is Goal 13 (Goal 12 is responsible consumption and production), and Goal 14 is life below water (life on land is Goal 15).
questions.h: 13 = climate (unlucky for the planet); 14 water, 15 land: sea before shore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the SDG India Index:
1. NITI Aayog is the nodal institution for overseeing the adoption of the SDGs in India.
2. The index was first launched in December 2018.
3. It is published by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NITI Aayog prepares and publishes the SDG India Index, scoring states and union territories from 0 to 100. MoSPI develops the national indicator framework used to monitor progress but does not publish the index.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Scheme : Sustainable Development Goal most directly served
1. Jal Jeevan Mission : Goal 6 (Clean water and sanitation)
2. Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana : Goal 7 (Affordable and clean energy)
3. Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) : Goal 11 (Sustainable cities and communities)
4. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao : Goal 13 (Climate action)
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao targets the declining child sex ratio and girls' education, so it maps to Goal 5 (gender equality), not climate action. The other three pairings are direct.
questions.s: NITI Aayog, SDG India Index; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding estimation of poverty in India:
1. The Tendulkar Committee (2009) continued to base the poverty line solely on the calorie norms of 2400 and 2100 calories for rural and urban areas.
2. The Rangarajan Committee (2014) estimated a higher poverty ratio for 2011-12 than the Tendulkar Committee.
3. The Lakdawala Committee (1993) recommended that state-specific poverty lines be used.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Tendulkar moved away from the pure calorie norm to a consumption basket that includes private spending on health and education. Rangarajan's line gave about 29.5 percent against Tendulkar's 21.9 percent for 2011-12, and Lakdawala introduced state-specific lines.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Gini coefficient of zero indicates perfect equality of income distribution.
2. A Gini coefficient of one indicates perfect equality of income distribution.
3. The further the Lorenz curve is from the line of equality, the greater the inequality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Gini coefficient is the ratio of the area between the Lorenz curve and the equality line to the whole area under the line, so 0 is equality and 1 is the extreme where one person holds everything.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q: The Kuznets curve postulates that, as per capita income of a country grows,
o: income inequality first falls and then rises, giving a U-shaped relationship
unemployment falls as inflation rises, giving a downward-sloping relationship
tax revenue first rises and then falls as tax rates are increased
income inequality first rises and then falls, giving an inverted-U relationship
questions.e: Kuznets argued that early industrialisation widens the gap between the modern and traditional sectors, and later spread of education and redistribution narrows it. The last two options describe the Phillips and Laffer curves.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter
questions.h: Kuznets: inequality climbs the hill, then rolls down.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an economist and a contribution is correctly matched?
o: Arthur Lewis : Dual-sector model in which surplus labour moves from agriculture to the modern sector
W.W. Rostow : Growth determined by the savings rate and the capital-output ratio
Robert Solow : Growth driven by endogenous technological change within the firm
Harrod and Domar : Growth with diminishing returns to capital and exogenous technology
questions.e: Rostow gave stages of growth; the savings-rate and capital-output logic is Harrod-Domar; the Solow model treats technology as exogenous, with diminishing returns to capital. Endogenous growth theory is associated with Romer and Lucas.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following stages in Rostow's stages of economic growth:
1. Take-off
2. Drive to maturity
3. Preconditions for take-off
4. Age of high mass consumption
Which one of the following is the correct sequence of these stages?
questions.e: Rostow's order is: traditional society, preconditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity, and the age of high mass consumption. The take-off is the decisive jump when investment rises sharply and growth becomes self-sustaining.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter
questions.h: Traditional - Preconditions - Take-off - Drive to maturity - High mass consumption: 'Plane: prepare, take off, cruise, land in comfort'.

questions.q: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), developed by Morris D. Morris, is based on
o: basic literacy, infant mortality and life expectancy at age one
literacy, infant mortality and per capita income
life expectancy at birth, gross enrolment and GDP per capita
maternal mortality, school attendance and life expectancy at age one
questions.e: PQLI looks only at outcomes, not income. Its three indicators are literacy rate, infant mortality and life expectancy at age one, each scaled from 0 to 100.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a pillar of Bhutan's Gross National Happiness?
questions.e: The four pillars are sustainable and equitable socio-economic development, environmental conservation, preservation and promotion of culture, and good governance. Bhutan deliberately places well-being above output expansion.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q: According to the Harrod-Domar framework, an economy with a saving (investment) rate of 30 percent of GDP and an incremental capital-output ratio of 4 will grow at about
questions.e: Growth rate = investment rate / ICOR = 30/4 = 7.5 percent. Lower ICOR (more efficient capital) or a higher saving rate raises growth.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Inequality-adjusted HDI discounts the HDI for inequality in the distribution of each dimension.
2. The Inequality-adjusted HDI can exceed the HDI of a country with very low inequality.
3. The Planetary pressures-adjusted HDI adjusts the HDI for carbon dioxide emissions and material footprint.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IHDI equals HDI only under perfect equality and is below it otherwise, so it can never exceed the HDI. The PHDI, introduced in the 2020 report, deducts for per capita CO2 emissions and material footprint.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q:
Statement-I: The poverty headcount ratio does not capture how far below the poverty line the poor are.
Statement-II: The headcount ratio treats every person below the line as equally poor, whatever the shortfall from the line.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because the ratio only counts heads, a household just below the line and one in destitution weigh the same. The poverty gap ratio and Sen's index were designed to capture depth and distribution.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter
